### W11.3 · Fix: the web page's Edit goal changes text the page never shows, and the title it does show stays uneditable
Parent: W11.2
Status: open
Approach: web.py `task_json` sets `goal` to `t["name"]` (the `# W11 · <name>` title line) and only falls back to the Goal text when there is no name; web/index.html draws that as the task's `<h2>` (line ~455) and the task list shows it too (`it.goal`). The new `goal_text` is used only to prefill the Edit goal textarea. So on any task with a title line (every task `new_task` writes, and W11 itself) saving a new goal changes `## Goal` but nothing on the page, and the words the author sees as the item, its title, still cannot be edited from the web (only the project title has `/api/title`). Check: POST /api/goal on a task with a title, then read `task_json(task)["goal"]` and the page; it is unchanged. Settle it by deciding what "the item" is on the page and making its edit visible: either let the Edit dialog also rewrite the title line (add a `name` field to `tree.set_goal` or a sibling `set_name` that rewrites only the `# <id> · <name>` line, refuses empty or multi-line, with tests in test_tree.py and test_web.py), or show the Goal text on the task page so the saved edit is seen. State whichever is chosen as a Hypothesis with its page. Also, in the same node: `tree.set_goal` picks `home_path` (first part with a `## Goal` heading) while `combine` picks the first part with a non-empty goal, so a default part with an empty `## Goal` and a branch part holding the real goal edits the wrong file; make set_goal edit the part `combine` reads the goal from (`load(task)["home"]`), with a test.

### W22.3 · Fix: the terminal footer no longer draws "w stop walk" in red
Parent: W22.2
Status: open
Approach: scripts/tui.py `draw_footer` (~line 3909) picks the red/bold "state that wants seeing" style with `loud = label.isupper()`. W22.2 lowercased "w STOP WALK" to "w stop walk" (line ~3747), so `"stop walk".isupper()` is now False and the walk-running state in the footer is drawn in the plain chrome colour instead of red: a behaviour regression the lowercasing introduced, which no test covers. Replace the case test with an explicit signal (e.g. have `footer` mark the segment, or compare the label to "stop walk" / a named constant, or return a loud flag alongside the text), update the docstring at ~3899 that still says "A capitalised label is a state", and add a test that draws the footer with `walk_on` true and asserts the stop-walk label gets `curses.color_pair(1)`. Check: the test fails against the current code and passes after the fix; grep tui.py for other `isupper()`/case-based logic on display strings finds none left.

### W36.5 · Fix: reopening a chat whose first turn was interrupted before any transcript restarts that turn
Parent: W36.1
Status: open
Approach: In `scripts/chat.py`, `Chats.turn` keeps the planned session id after an interrupt only if a transcript file already exists, and `Chats.open` takes "a conversation has begun" to mean "the saved sid has a transcript, or the screen's chat is live". So when a page-run turn is interrupted before claude has written its transcript (an opening summary, or a first message, stopped within the first moments), `sid` stays empty, and the next `open(scope)` (the page closed and reopened, or `chatBegin`) sees "not began", starts the opening turn again, and clears the "Interrupted." note. Checked here with test_chat's stub (`CHAT_STUB_SLEEP=60`; `open("W1")`, `wait_for_agent`, `interrupt`, `settle` gives `[note Interrupted.]`; a second `open("W1")` returns `busy=True, messages=[]` with a new opening turn running). Also a first message stopped this way leaves its `pending` "you" bubble in the state while the next message, which starts a fresh session, drops it. Fix so that an interrupted turn is not silently redone on reopen: for example record in `Chats` (in memory is enough, or in the scope's `.json` record beside `sid`) that the opening was interrupted and make `open` skip the automatic opening turn then, until the author sends a message or presses New chat; and make the shown conversation after such an interrupt agree with what the next turn will resume (do not keep a "you" bubble for a message no session holds, or say it was not taken). Settle it with tests in `test_chat.py`: interrupt an opening turn with no transcript, call `open` again, and see no new turn and the note kept; and interrupt a first message with no transcript and see the state agree with the session the next send uses.

### W36.6 · Fix: a second Interrupt on a screen-run chat types a second Esc into the claude, which the code itself says would end it
Parent: W36.2
Status: open
Approach: In `scripts/ptyrelay.py`, `Relay.interrupt` types an Esc whenever `self.active` (output within the last 2.0 seconds). After the first Esc claude redraws ("Interrupted…"), so the agent stays `active` for up to two seconds after the stop, and the page does not stop a second press: for a screen-run chat `Chats.state` has `stopping=False` (it is only set for a page-run turn), so `chatDraw` re-enables `#chat-stop` straight after the first press (`$("#chat-stop").disabled = !!st.stopping`), and a double tap on a phone sends two Esc bytes in quick succession. The method's own docstring says "a second would end it" (an Esc at an idle claude clears the input, a second exits or opens its rewind menu). `test_ptyrelay.py` and `test_chat.py` test one interrupt, an idle one and a dropped queue, but not two in a row (the "twice is once" test covers only the page-run turn). Fix in the relay so that a second Esc is not typed until the output after the first one has gone quiet (for instance remember when the last Esc was typed and the output total then, and refuse another until the agent has been silent for QUIET seconds after it, or for a fixed window), logging the refusal, and in `Chats.interrupt` / the page show it as stopping meanwhile so the button is not offered again at once. Settle it with a `test_ptyrelay.py` test where the stand-in agent keeps writing after the first Esc: two `interrupt()` calls within the window deliver exactly one ESC.

### W36.7 · Hypothesis: a headless claude killed by SIGTERM leaves a session the next `--resume` accepts, and the Interrupted note text is claude's own
Parent: W36.1
Status: open
Approach: W36.1 rests on assumptions it did not state and could not settle (no claude binary here; the stub writes a clean transcript): (1) that `claude -p` stopped with SIGTERM mid-turn has already written the author's message to its transcript, and leaves a transcript that `claude --resume <sid>` accepts, including when it stopped between a tool call and its result (an orphan `tool_use`), so that `Chats.turn` may keep `planned` as the session and `send` may resume it; if it does not, the next message after an Interrupt fails with the agent's error instead of going on; (2) that an Esc-stopped turn is recorded in the transcript as a user line starting `[Request interrupted by user`, which `transcript_messages` turns into the "Interrupted." note (the one the screen's chat shows); if the text differs the note never shows for screen-run chats. The session that takes this up states both as a `Hypothesis:` on W36.1 (and on the transcript mapping), with its page, saying what would show them wrong: a real `claude -p` killed mid-turn whose next `--resume` errors or loses the message, and a real Esc-stopped transcript without that line. Add the evidence the documentation or a source gives (search for the transcript format and for resume of an interrupted session).

### W36.5 · Fix: a second Interrupt on a background chat types a second Esc
Parent: W36.2
Status: open
Approach: `ptyrelay.Relay.interrupt()` writes an ESC whenever `self.active` (output in the last 2 s). After the first Esc, claude redraws ("Interrupted") so it stays `active` for up to 2 s, and a second click, double-tap or a retry from the page (the Interrupt button is only disabled when `st.stopping`, which is set only for page-run turns, never for a chat on the screen) types a second Esc. The method's own docstring says a second Esc ends/changes the agent, and W36.4's "interrupt twice in a row" was only exercised for page-run turns (`test_chat` "twice is once"); there is no relay test of two interrupts. Fix: make a repeat a no-op until the agent has gone quiet after the Esc (e.g. remember `self.esc_at` and refuse to type another while `last_out` has not been quiet since, or within a fixed window), return False/log it, and have `Chats.interrupt`/the page not treat that as an error (button disabled or toast "already stopping"). Check in `test_ptyrelay.py` with the BUSY agent: two `interrupt()` calls in a row log exactly one `ESC`; after the agent is quiet and busy again, a new interrupt types one more.

### W36.4 · Hypothesis: a page-run turn killed with SIGTERM leaves a session that `--resume` accepts
Parent: W36.1
Status: open
Approach: W36.1 rests on an assumption it does not state as a Hypothesis. `Chats.interrupt` ends the page's `run.sh --chat-turn` process with SIGTERM (`interrupt_process` in `scripts/chat.py`), assuming (a) the signal reaches the claude process through run.sh's `exec` and whatever launcher `CLAUDE_CMD` is (a `nix run` wrapper may not pass it on), and (b) the transcript a `claude -p` killed mid-turn leaves (the author's question on record, no answer) is one `claude --resume <id>` accepts, so the next message continues it; `turn()` also now chooses the session id itself (`run_sid`) so a killed first turn can be kept. The tests use a stub shell that traps TERM and writes a one-line transcript, so neither is shown with a real claude (none is installed here). It would be wrong if the launcher swallows SIGTERM (the turn runs on until the timeout, and "Interrupted" is shown over a live agent) or if `--resume` refuses or drops the half-written session (the next send fails or loses the question). The session that takes this up states both as a Hypothesis on W36.1's page, with what would show each wrong (a real claude: Stop on a page chat, then check the process is gone and a following message resumes with the question in the transcript), and appends Evidence from whatever can be read or run (the launcher's argv in run.sh, claude's documented resume behaviour).

### W36.4 · Fix: a stale `stopped` entry makes the author's next message die at once
Parent: W36.1
Status: open
Approach: In `scripts/chat.py`, `Chats.turn()` discards the scope from `self.stopped` in its first `with self.lock:` block (after the agent has ended) but only pops `self.busy[scope]` in a second lock block, after `chatlog.log` and `save_sid`. `Chats.interrupt()` tests `scope in self.busy`, so a Stop that lands between the two blocks (for example the author taps Stop just as the answer arrives) adds the scope to `self.stopped` and nothing ever removes it. The next `send()` starts a turn, `Chats.started()` sees the scope in `stopped` and calls `interrupt_process` on the new agent immediately, so the author's following message is killed and shown as "Interrupted" with no answer. Fix: clear `self.stopped` for the scope where a turn begins (in `send()` and in `open()` when it starts the opening turn, under the lock, beside `self.stops.discard`), and/or only discard it and pop `busy` in one lock block so `interrupt()` cannot see busy after the discard. Check: in `test_chat.py`, with a stub agent, call `interrupt` after the first lock block has run (for instance patch `chatlog.log` to call `interrupt` when it logs the "answered" line), then `send` again and assert the second turn is answered and not interrupted.

### W36.4 · Fix: interrupting a chat's first turn loses the conversation
Parent: W36.1
Status: open
Approach: In `scripts/chat.py` `Chats.turn`, a chat with no record has `sid == ""`; `run.sh --chat-turn` then makes its own uuid (`--session-id "${CHAT_SID:-$(python3 ... uuid4)}"`, run.sh ~line 320) and `turn()` only learns it from the JSON the agent prints at the end (`new_sid = out.get("session_id")`).
